attackType: Ransomware Lateral Propagation & Remote Code Execution
title: Critical Port 445 (SMB / CIFS) Exposed
description: Device has SMB / CIFS open. Potential attack vector: WannaCry, NotPetya, EternalBlue, Lateral Ransomware Propagation
recommendation: Block port 445 on WAN and internal boundaries. Disable legacy SMBv1 and enforce SMB signing/encryption.
remediationSteps: Immediately block Port 445 on perimeter firewalls and router WAN interfaces.
Disable legacy SMBv1 in Windows (Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol).
Enforce SMB signing and SMB encryption for internal file shares.
Isolate internal file sharing to dedicated private management VLANs.

attackType: Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution & Automated Brute Force
title: Critical Port 3389 (RDP (Remote Desktop)) Exposed
description: Device has RDP (Remote Desktop) open. Potential attack vector: BlueKeep, Automated credential brute-force, Ransomware deployment
recommendation: Never expose RDP directly to network. Restrict access through VPN, require NLA, and enable MFA.
remediationSteps: Never expose RDP (Port 3389) directly to public Internet or untrusted subnets.
Require secure WireGuard / OpenVPN or SSH Bastion tunnel to access remote desktops.
Enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA) on Windows System Properties.
Configure Account Lockout Policies to prevent automated password dictionary attacks.

attackType: RPC Buffer Overflow & Remote System Enumeration
title: High Risk Port 135 (MS RPC / EPMAP) Open
description: Exposed MS RPC / EPMAP service is susceptible to: Blaster worm, unauthenticated RPC buffer overflows, system reconnaissance
recommendation: Block port 135 at firewall. Filter inbound RPC from untrusted network segments.
remediationSteps: Block Port 135 on perimeter router and host firewall.
Filter inbound RPC requests and restrict to authorized domain controllers only.

firewallCmd.powershell: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Block Port 135 (MS RPC)" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 135 -Protocol TCP -Action Block

cve: xp_cmdshell Remote Code Execution & SA Dictionary Attacks
attackType: Database Takeover & OS Command Execution
title: High Risk Port 1433 (MS SQL Server) Open
description: Exposed MS SQL Server service is susceptible to: Automated SA user brute-force, xp_cmdshell command execution
recommendation: Change default port, disable SA account, bind to internal interfaces only.
remediationSteps: Disable or rename default SA administrator account and enforce complex passwords.
Disable xp_cmdshell extended stored procedures in SQL Server Management Studio.
Restrict SQL Server TCP listening to internal application server IP addresses.

cve: CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) / Mirai
attackType: Cleartext Credential Eavesdropping & IoT Botnet Takeover
title: Critical Port 23 (Telnet) Exposed
description: Device has Telnet open. Potential attack vector: Cleartext credential eavesdropping, Mirai IoT botnet propagation
recommendation: Disable Telnet daemon completely. Migrate to SSH (Port 22) with key authentication.
remediationSteps: Stop and permanently disable the Telnet service daemon.
Migrate all remote management to SSH (Port 22) with Ed25519 cryptographic keys.
Change default manufacturer credentials on all network routers and switches.

firewallCmd.powershell: Stop-Service -Name "TlntSvr" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Block Port 23 (Telnet)" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 23 -Protocol TCP -Action Block

description: Device has SMB / CIFS open. Potential attack vector: WannaCry, NotPetya, EternalBlue, Lateral Ransomware Propagation
recommendation: Block port 445 on WAN and internal boundaries. Disable legacy SMBv1 and enforce SMB signing/encryption.
remediationSteps: Immediately block Port 445 on perimeter firewalls and router WAN interfaces.
Disable legacy SMBv1 in Windows (Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol).
Enforce SMB signing and SMB encryption for internal file shares.
Isolate internal file sharing to dedicated private management VLANs.

attackType: RPC Buffer Overflow & Remote System Enumeration
title: High Risk Port 135 (MS RPC / EPMAP) Open
description: Exposed MS RPC / EPMAP service is susceptible to: Blaster worm, unauthenticated RPC buffer overflows, system reconnaissance
recommendation: Block port 135 at firewall. Filter inbound RPC from untrusted network segments.
remediationSteps: Block Port 135 on perimeter router and host firewall.
Filter inbound RPC requests and restrict to authorized domain controllers only.

firewallCmd.powershell: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Block Port 135 (MS RPC)" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 135 -Protocol TCP -Action Block

attackType: Relay Attacks, NTLM Hash Harvesting & Man-in-the-Middle
title: High Risk Port 139 (NetBIOS Session) Open
description: Exposed NetBIOS Session service is susceptible to: NetBIOS name enumeration, session hijacking, relay attacks
recommendation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP in Network Adapter IPv4 Advanced settings.
remediationSteps: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP in Network Adapter IPv4 Advanced WINS settings.
Block Inbound Port 139 on all external and untrusted interfaces.

attackType: Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution & Automated Brute Force
title: Critical Port 3389 (RDP (Remote Desktop)) Exposed
description: Device has RDP (Remote Desktop) open. Potential attack vector: BlueKeep, Automated credential brute-force, Ransomware deployment
recommendation: Never expose RDP directly to network. Restrict access through VPN, require NLA, and enable MFA.
remediationSteps: Never expose RDP (Port 3389) directly to public Internet or untrusted subnets.
Require secure WireGuard / OpenVPN or SSH Bastion tunnel to access remote desktops.
Enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA) on Windows System Properties.
Configure Account Lockout Policies to prevent automated password dictionary attacks.
